ref.name: Forms
steps: Red X - Non flyable condition (panel removed, tire worn out of limits, -21 equipment that is not normally installed, etc). The aircraft is considered unsafe or unserviceable, non-airworthy or unknown status/lack of accountability of special inspection/time change item requirements has been identified and will not be flown or used until the unsatisfactory condition is corrected and/or the symbol is cleared. Aircraft may be operated (but not flown) as necassary to troubleshoot or repair the discrepancy.

Red Dash - Flyable condition (inspections, accessory replacement, ops checks, etc). The presence of the Red Dash symbol indicates the condition of the equipment is unknown and a more serious condition may exist.

Red Diagonal -  Flyable condition (servicing). The Red Diagonal indicates that a discrepancy exists on equipment, but is not sufficiently urgent or dangerous to warrant its grounding or discontinued use.
Red W - Indicates that a ICBM (Intercontinental Ballistic Missile) is inoperative for its intended use and requires careful attention
Red C - Indicated the A/C is contaminated by a chemical, biological, radiological agent, environmental,or infestation (rodents)
Black Dash - No discrepancies exist (used in Hs)

ref.name: Troubleshooting
steps:
Delta-P extends during launch (29FI-00-1, Fault Code: XD)
- Case drain, return, or pressure: Reset If good, inspect filter after flight and document extension. If cannot be reset, document and inspect after flight. 
- Pressure: Reset, if good, document extension and inspect after flight. If cannot be reset, shut down, inspect filer (replace it)

<6 Fuel pump lights
- Remove door 3308
- Unscrew black lense cap (ensure the bulb comes with it)
- Switch with a known working bulb
- If it still does not light up: shutdown
- If it does light up, note the bulb will need to be replaced, close 3308. 

- Some lights may not be on if fuel is low.

BIT fail
- Cycle flight controls until A/B system hydro is above 55 degrees.
- If fails again, cycle until 70-75 degrees
- If it still fails, call for a red ball

2697/-451/19615.data: Contains warning lights and controls related to flight control functions

2697/-451/19615.name: DIGITAL BACKUP
2697/-451/19615.data: Selects backup software program within the FLCC

2697/-451/19615.name: ALT FLAPS
2697/-451/19615.data: Flaperon operation controlled by landing gear handle (NORM) or extended regardless of landng gear handle position (EXTEND)

2697/-451/19615.name: MANUAL TF FLYUP
2697/-451/19615.data: Apart of the TF (Terrain Following) radar system. When disabled, the autopilot commands a max climb to ensure terrain clearance.

2697/-451/19615.name: LE FLAPS
2697/-451/19615.data: When in the LOCK position, the LEFs do not move regardless of AOA. When in AUTO, the LEFs are changed depending on AOA and air speed.

2697/-451/19615.name: FLCS
2697/-451/19615.data: Performs FLCS reset when set to reset. Resets CADC, FLCS FAULT, and MASTER CAUTION lights and clears PFLs if fault clears.

2697/-451/19615.name: BIT
2697/-451/19615.data: Commands BIT if weight is on MLG and wheel speed is less than 28 knots.

2697/-451/19615.name: RUN/FAIL Lights
2697/-451/19615.data: RUN (green) shows the BIT is running. FAIL (red) shows failed FLCS BIT

2691/-456/19679.data: Controls yaw, pitch, and roll trim

2691/-456/19679.name: ROLL TRIM
2691/-456/19679.data: Controls roll trim with a indicator showing which wing is down

2691/-456/19679.name: PITCH TRIM
2691/-456/19679.data: Controls pitch trim with an indicator

2691/-456/19679.name: TRIM/AP DISC
2691/-456/19679.data: In NORM, energizes stick TRIM button and permins autopilot engagement. In DISC, Deenergizes stick TRIM button, prevents autopilot engagement, and deactivates trim motors (manual trim wheels still work)

2808/-453/19626.name: IFF MASTER
2808/-453/19626.data:
OFF - Removes power from IFF equipment and zeroizes mode 4 settings unless HOLD function has been used. The knob must be lifted to position to or from OFF 
 STBY - The equipment is turned on and warmed up but does not transmit 
 LOW - Same as NORM 
 EMER - The knob must be lifted to EMER.

2808/-453/19626.name: M-4 CODE
2808/-453/19626.data:
ZERO - Zeroizes mode 4 settings whenever IFF MASTER knob is not OFF 
 A/B - Permits code selection via upfront controls or via IFF MODE 4 REPLY switch when C & I knob is in backup 
 HOLD - Both code settings can be retained after flight by placoing the IFF M4 CODE switch to HOLD momentarily priot to placing the IFF MASTER knob to OFF or removing power

2808/-453/19626.name: C & I
2808/-453/19626.data:
BACKUP - Provides alternate operation of the UHF and IFF 
 UFC - Normal control of communications, navigation, and IFF

2808/-453/19626.name: ENABLE
2808/-453/19626.data:
Only available when mode selection in BACKUP 

 M3/MS - Modes 3/A and S enabled in backup 
 OFF - Modes 1, 3/A and S disabled in backup 
 M1/M3 - Modes 1 and 3/A enabled in backup

2808/-453/19626.name: MODE 1 / MODE 3
2808/-453/19626.data:
The MODE 1 code selector levers are incremented/decremented to select the two-digit code displayed in the readout windows. The two left-most windows display the mode 1 code digits when the C & I knob is in BACKUP 

 The Mode 3/A code selector levers are incremented/decremented to select the two-digit code displayed in the readout windows. The two right-most windows display the two most significant mode 3/A backup code digits when the C & I knob is in BACKUP. The two least significant digits are always set to zero. For example, if the windows are set to 77, the transmitted mode 3/A code is 7700.

2808/-453/19626.name: MODE 4 REPLY
2808/-453/19626.data:
Used when C & I is in BACKUP. 
 OUT - MODE 4 operation is disabled. A - Enabled mode 4 and selects preset code for A

2808/-453/19626.name: MODE 4 MONITOR
2808/-453/19626.data:
The IFF MODE 4 MONITOR switch permits audio monitor of mode 4 replies when the C & I knob is in BACKUP 

 AUDIO -  Monitoring of mode 4 interrogations is provided by an audio tone on the intercom. An audio tone of 0 to 1000 Hz is generated when the transponder is not replying to valid mode 4 interrogations. The frequency of the tone depends on the number of interrogations received 
 OUT - Disables audio monitor

2811/-466/19708.name: FLASH STEADY

2811/-466/19708.name: FUSELAGE

2811/-466/19708.name: AERIAL REFUELING

2910/-453/19579.data: Emergency system that provides hydraulic and electric power in case of generator, hydraulic, or engine failures.

2910/-453/19579.name: HYDRAZN light
2910/-453/19579.data: An amber colored light that illuminates when the EPU is commanding hydrazine (whether its available or not)

2910/-453/19579.name: AIR light
2910/-453/19579.data: An amber colored light when the EPU has been commanded to run with the EPU safety pin removed (in bleed air mode)

2910/-453/19579.name: EPU run light
2910/-453/19579.data: A small unmarked green light that illuminates when the turbine speed is within the proper range and EPU-driven hydraulic pump discharges pressure above 2000 psi

2910/-453/19579.name: EPU
2910/-453/19579.data:
OFF - Prevents EPU operation on the ground (WOW switches), terminates EPU operation in flight exept during main and standy generator failures. 
 NORM - System is armed for automatic operation except for when WOW is active 
 ON - Commands EPU to run regardless of failure conditions.

2920/-458/19631.data: Controls the electric system and contains warning lights

2920/-458/19631.name: MAIN PWR
2920/-458/19631.data:
MAIN PWR - Allows external power 
 BATT - powers specific components with battery 
 OFF - No power

2920/-458/19631.name: ELEC CAUTION RESET
2920/-458/19631.data: Resets resettable overcurrent protection units and ELEC SYS caution light and clears MASTER CAUTION light. Resets maind and standby generators

2920/-458/19631.name: FLCS PWR TEST
2920/-458/19631.data:
TEST - tests FLCC power output 
 NORM - Tests EPU PMG power availability during EPU/GEN test on ground 
 MAINT - For MX use on ground. Inpoperative in flight

2920/-458/19631.name: Indicator lights
2920/-458/19631.data:
FLCS PMG - Amber light. If in flight, it means none of the FLCS branches are receiving power from FLCS PMG. If on ground, FLCS PMG power is not available at one or more FLCS branches. light is delayed 60 seconds after initial NLG WOW 
 MAIN GEN - Shows external power or main generator not connected to one or both nonessential AC buses 
 EPU GEN - Shows EPU has been commanded on but the EPU generator is not providing power to both emergency AC buses. The light does not function when EPU is in OFF (WOW) and the engine is running 
 STBY GEN - Indicates standby generator power is not available 
 EPU PMG - Shows the EPU has been commanded on but EPU PMG power is not available to all branches of the FLCS 
 ACFT BATT - (FAIL) if in flight indicates A/C battery failure (less than 20 volts). If on ground, indicates the A/C battery fail or charging fail. (TO FLCS) If in flight, shows battery power is going to one or more FLCS branches and voltage is 25 volts or less. If on ground, indicates the battery power is going to one or more FLCS branches. (FLCS RLY) Shows the voltage on one or more of the four FLCS branches connected to the A/C battery is inadequate (below 20 volts) or that one or more FLCS branches are not connected to the battery 
 ELEC SYS - Illuminates in conjuction with any of the above lights 
 FLCS PWR - Green lights (A, B, C, and D) lights up to indicate proper power output of FLCC during FLCS power tests

 TGT SEP - On full time only when power to RWR

ON - On when selected. Self-test shows two test screens.

U - On when RWR has power and these are true: UNKNOWN mode has been selected by the player or UNKNOWN mode is not engaged but the RWR detects unknown type radars painting ownership.

3351/25/19898.data: Provides a visual heads up indication of aircraft AOA by illuminating the symbols individually or in combinations. The indexer lights display AOA correction (based on ~13 degrees AOA). This correction may be used during landing approaches as visual direction toward optimal landing AOA. Operates continuously with the LG handle UP or DN

3431/-162/19855.name: FCR
3431/-162/19855.data: Fire Control Radar. Air to air radar display

3431/-162/19855.data: Horizontal Situation Display. Map like display that shows navigation, datalink, and threats

3431/-162/19855.name: HARM
3431/-162/19855.data: High Speed Anit-radiation Missile. When using AGM-88

3227/-9/19995.data: The UFC (Upfront Controls) are comprised of 3 components: the ICP (Integrated Control Panel), the DED (Data Entry Display), and the PFLD (Pilot Fault List Display). Handles communication, navigation, and identification (CNI) functions. The UFC divides controls into two sections. With commonly used functions on the ICP, and less commonly used controls into two side consoles. The ICP is quick access to commonly used functions, like overrides and priority features through a single push-button interface.

3343/-253/19995.name: Airspeed
3343/-253/19995.data: Shows both knots and mach readings (80 - 850 knots, 0.5 - 2.2 mach). The reading is supplied by total and static pressure supplied by the pitot static system.

3343/-253/19995.name: Altimeter
3343/-253/19995.data:
The altimeter reads MSL (Mean Sea Level) and has two modes of operation. It can be electrically powered (set to ELECT) from the CADC (Central Air Data Computer) or pneumatically powered (set to PNEU) by the static ports. The primary position is ELECT and PNEU is secondary. If the CADC or altimeter servo malfunction, the PNEU mode is automatically set and the PNEU flag appears on the face of the altimeter. The PNEU flag may also apper during high G maneuvers or accelerating or decelerating through transonic regions. 
 The barometric setting knob (located on the bottom left hand side of the altimeter) is used to set the desired altimeter setting. The barometric setting of the altimeter is electrically transmitted to the CADC as a manual input correction for the pressure altitude displayed on the HUD. The baromtric setting is shown in inches of mercury. 
 The operating range is -1000 to 80,000 feet MSL

3343/-253/19995.name: VVI
3343/-253/19995.data:
Vertical Velocity Indicator. 
 Displays rate of climb/descent provided by the CADC and has a operating range of 6,000 feet per minute climb or dive.

3343/-253/19995.name: ADI
3343/-253/19995.data:
Attitude Director Indicator 
 Displays pitch and roll attitude information from the INS. It is not limited to a set operating range and shows any aircraft accurately. The turn rate needle is driven by the rate gyroscope transmitter. The pitch trim knob is used to adjust the attitude sphere to the desired pitch attitude. The OFF-warning flag may indicate failure of either the INS or the ADI. A momentary OFF and/or AUX flag, even with proper attitude being displayed, may indicate impending failure of the ADI or INS data to the ADI. The GS warning flag indicates that the glide slope deviation bar is unreliable. The LOC warning flag indicates that the localizer signal is unreliable. The AUX warning flag signifies that the INS has failed or is operating in a less precise attitude condition and that HSI heading must be set to a known heading by the HDG knob on the HSI.

3343/-253/19995.name: HSI
3343/-253/19995.data:
Horizontal Situation Indicator 
 Shows direction the A/C is pointing, where the next waypoint or navigation station is, and shows if the A/C is left or right of the desired course. 
 Refer to FALCON BMS SYSTEMS MANUAL 29.7 for a more in depth description.

3306/-5/20101.data: Apart of the UFC. The DED and PFLD have the capacity to display up to five rows of alphanumeric characters and symbols, with each row accommodating up to 24 characters. Their display screens consist of a high resolution dot matrix, containing 64 pixels per linear inch. Overall, the display surface encompasses 192 columns by 64 rows of pixels, providing a visually detailed interface

3437/-84/20165.data: Displays the flow of fuel going into the engine in PPH (pounds per hour)

3393/-168/20224.data: Shows gauges related to the engine

3393/-168/20224.name: NOZ POS
3393/-168/20224.data: Shows the position of the augmentor/nozzle using a percentage value. 100% means nozzle is fully open

3393/-168/20224.name: RPM
3393/-168/20224.data: Shows the RPM in a percent value. Data supplied by the engine alternator.

3393/-168/20224.name: FTIT
3393/-168/20224.data:
Fan Turbine Inlet Tempeture 
 Displays an average FTIT in degrees C. The indicator has a range of 200 - 1,200 degress C

3266/-325/20340.data: Shows hydraulic pressure of A and B system. If both systems drop below 1000 psi in flight, the EPU activates.

3145/-439/20344.name: L/R HDPT
3145/-439/20344.data: Provides power to left and right targetting pods (SNIPER, LANTIRN, HTS)

3145/-439/20344.name: FCR
3145/-439/20344.data: When powered up the FCR enters a Power ON Built-In Test (PO BIT) mode, visible on the MFD. The BIT lasts about 3 minutes after which the radar is set to standby, unless previously set to a specific mode. The PO BIT can't be interrupted in the middle of the test. The only way to 'truly' interrupt it is to turn the radar off.

3145/-439/20344.name: RDR ALT
3145/-439/20344.data: With the switch in OFF the radar altimeter is inoperative. In STBY the radar altimeter is placed in standby mode (used on the ground to avoid frying the crew chief). In RDR ALT the radar altimeter is fully operative. RALT BIT is implemented and visible from the MFD TEST page (OSB 7). When the radar altimeter is active the radar altitude can be read in the HUD in the box preceded by the letter R. Certain conditions must be met for the Radar altitude to be displayed. Those conditions depend on altitude: Low level the RALT will blank past 30 degree pitch and approximately 90 degree bank. High altitude the RALT will blank above 10 degree pitch and approximately 75 degree bank. Note the comma that remains displayed, even when the altitude is blanked.

3101/-445/20335.name: VV
3101/-445/20335.data:
VV/VAH - in addition to the vertical velocity scale there is also a bank angle (15/30/45/60) indicator on the FPM. 
 VAH - There is a roll indicator below the heading tape (unless you have chosen to display the DED or PFL in the HUD) with 10/20/30deg and 45 deg cues 
 OFF - no scales or bank/roll indication is displayed

3101/-445/20335.name: ATT
3101/-445/20335.data:
ATT/FPM - Both the pitch ladder and flight path marker are displayed. 
 FPM - Only flight path marker 
 OFF - Neither pitch ladder nor FPM is displayed

3101/-445/20335.name: DED DATA
3101/-445/20335.data:
DED DATA - The DED is displayed in the HUD 
 PFL - The pilot Fault List is displayed on the bottom of the HUD 
 OFF - Neither DED or PFL is displayed to the HUD

3101/-445/20335.name: SPD
3101/-445/20335.data:
CAS - Speed tape shows the calibrated airspeed. CAS indicated airspeed (IAS) corrected for position and instrument error 
 TAS - speed tape shows true airspeed (TAS). TAS is CAS corrected for pressure altitude, so it is the airspeed in the air mass at this altitude. 
 GND SPD - HUD shows the speed over the ground. Groundspeed is TAS corrected for winds. A caret is also displayed on the heading tape. The caret means the system is now in wind correcred ground track as oppoed to showing heading as magnetic track

3101/-445/20335.name: ALT
3101/-445/20335.data:
RADAR - the altitude tape indicates radar altitude 
 BARO - the altitude tape indicates barometric altitude 
 AUTO - the altitude tape indicates barometric altitude above 1500 feet and switches to radar altitude below 1500 feet

3101/-445/20335.name: HUD BRT
3101/-445/20335.data: Adapts the HUD brightness based on time of day

3032/-452/20337.name: PRIMARY INST PNL
3032/-452/20337.data: Lights up forward instrument panel and right auxillary console lighting

3032/-452/20337.name: DATA ENTRY DISPLAY
3032/-452/20337.data: Controls brightness of the Data Entry Display (DED) and Pilot Fault List Display (PFLD)

2712/-450/20429.name: IFF
2712/-450/20429.data:
UPPER - Upper antenna is used to receive and reply to interrogation signals 
 LOWER - Lower antenna is used to receive and reply to interrogation signals 
 NORM - Cycle between upper and lower antennas

2712/-450/20429.name: UHF
2712/-450/20429.data:
UPPER - Upper antenna is used to receive and transmit signals 
 LOWER - Lower antenna is used to recive and transmit signals 
 NORM - Cycles between upper and lower antennas

2767/-452/20429.data:
Three position switch that dictates the state of the inlet anti ice rod. 

 ON - Heater is on 
 AUTO - Uses tempeture to check if ice can form 
 OFF - Heater is off

2629/-449/20415.name: FLOW
2629/-449/20415.data: Shows if oxygen is flowing (white means flowing, black means no flow)

2629/-449/20415.name: OXYGEN SUPPLY PRESSURE
2629/-449/20415.data: Shows PSI of oxygen from 0 - 500 psi. If pilot experiences 500 psi of oxygen pressure to the mask, he may explode.

2629/-449/20415.name: RED LEVER
2629/-449/20415.data:
EMER - Starts flow of oxygen for emergency (more oxygen than normal flight) 
 NORM - Normal flight breathing 
 TEST MASK - Tests the mask (spring loaded to NORM)

2629/-449/20415.name: WHITE LEVER
2629/-449/20415.data:
100% - Pure oxygen 
 NORM - Oxygen mixed with outside air

2629/-449/20415.name: SUPPLY
2629/-449/20415.data:
PBG - Pressure Breathing for Gs (supplies higher pressure when under Gs) 
 ON - Normal pressure 
 OFF - No Oxygen

2733/-457/20375.name: MAP
2733/-457/20375.data: Is not wired, has no function but can be moved

3181/-273/19999.name: EJECTION HANDLE
3181/-273/19999.data:
Requires ~50 pounds of force to pull and requires the seat safety lever to be down. 
 If the ejection handle is pulled while seat is still pinned, when the seat becomes armed after the pilot sets it, the seat will eject.

3181/-273/19999.name: CANOPY JETTISON
3181/-273/19999.data: Located on the left side right next to the side wall. This is used in case of non-lethal crash where the pilot survived but did not eject. For the system to activate, the safety pin must be removed and the handle pulled.

3181/-273/19999.name: SURVIVAL KIT
3181/-273/19999.data:
This is located within the ejection seat. It contains a locator beacon, cold weather kit (poncho, sleeping bag, gloves), water filteration kit, knife/multi-tool, GAU-5A Rifle (5.56 rifle that breaks down) or sidearm, and a life raft. 
 Upon deployment, the survival kit drops under the seat and hangs 20-30 feet to ensure it lands before the seat.

3181/-273/19999.name: CHUTE RELEASE
3181/-273/19999.data: If parachute fails to release, the manual chute release lever can be used to deploy the parachute.

3416/-78/20117.data: The Standby Attitude Indicator (SAI) is a self-contained, electrically powered vertical gyroscope that mechanically positions the attitude sphere of the indicator to display aircraft pitch and roll attitudes. Located on the indicated is a PULL TO CAGE tab to manually cage the indicator. If caging is required, the aircraft should be flown wings level, constant altitude, and at an AOA of approximately +4 degrees. Since the SAI is mounted in the instrument panel at an angle, it indicates a pitch angle of 4 degrees less than the ADI when pitch trim knobs on both indicators are set at the pitch trim index.

3325/-269/20288.data:
Shows the fuel load with two needles. One state AL (Aft Left) and FR (Forward Right) showing the fuel load of the two engine-fed reservoirs. 
 Within the indicator is a totalizer that shows the total amount of fuel in pounds

3352/30/20101.data: Air Refuel and Nose Wheel Steering warning lights

3352/30/20101.name: AR/NWS
3352/30/20101.data:
AR light can come on for the door not opening or closing properly, position disagrees with the switch, or system detects other type of malfunction. 
 The NWS light can come on because NWS fails, system disengaged unexpectedly, or there is a fault in the steering control. 
 They share the same light to save space on this panel. AR is for the air, NWS is for the ground. They should never be on at the same time.

3352/30/20101.name: RDY
3352/30/20101.data: Shows the A/C is ready for air refueling

3352/30/20101.name: DISC
3352/30/20101.data: Shows the aircraft is disconnected from the tanker.

3088/-439/20412.name: NUCLEAR CONSENT
3088/-439/20412.data:
OFF - Normal position 
 ARM/REL - Normal nuclear delivery sequence 
 REL ONLY - Bypasses the arming step and allows only release consent

3256/-344/20261.data: If any of these light are on (along with some other warning lights around the cockpit), the MASTER CAUTION light will illuminate

3256/-344/20261.name: FLCS FAULT
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when FLCC reports a caution level PFL item which requires pilot action, FLCS BIT bis communication failure, single static or impact pressure failures, pitot tube icing (will also show really low airspeed), and any caution-level FLCS PFL item

3256/-344/20261.name: ELEC SYS
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminated when any electrical system detects a malfunction requiring pilot action. Includes main gen, standby gen, battery, electrical buses and controls circruitry

3256/-344/20261.name: PROBE HEAT
3256/-344/20261.data: When a failure occurs in the probe heat system including the pitot tube, AOA probes, and air data probe.

3256/-344/20261.name: C ADC
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the CADC fails or provides invalid air data. Aircraft systems that depend on the CADC information may receive degraded or incorrect data. The failure is reported through the caution light and associated system messages located on the PFLD

3256/-344/20261.name: STORES CONFIG
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates to alert the pilot that there is unsafe conditions for landing regarding external stores. Examples include external stores remain on stations that should be empty for landing (e.g. wing tanks being mostly empty), the aircraft landing configuration conflicts with the currwntly loaded stores. Landing could cause structural damage or exceed clearence limits.

3256/-344/20261.name: ATF NOT ENGAGED
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the Automatic Terrain Following mode is not engaged when it should be. Conditions that cause this light include terrain following radar operating but the ATF mode is not engaged (this warns the pilot that it is not following terrain so pilot control is required)

3256/-344/20261.name: FWD FUEL LOW
3256/-344/20261.data: Indicates that the fuel in the forward fuselage fuel cells decreases to a concerningly low level. The light illuminates when the fuel quantity in the forward fuselage tank group decreases to ~400 pounds or less

3256/-344/20261.name: AFT FUEL LOW
3256/-344/20261.data: Displays when the fuel quantity in the aft fuselage fuel cells decreases to a low level. The light illuminates when the fuel quantity in the aft fuselage tank group decreases to ~250 pounds or less

3256/-344/20261.name: ENGINE FAULT
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the Digital Engine Controls (DEC) detects a malfunction in the engine control system. Caused by engine control sensors, DEC fail, engine control signal faults, or engine control system internal malfunction.

3256/-344/20261.name: SEC
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the engine control is set to SEC (secondary) instead of the standard PRI (primary) mode. Conditions that cause this: DEC fail, engine control sensor failure, or engine control signal failure. SEC mode causes engine thrust response to be reduced, engine acceleration characteristics change, and some automatic engine protections are not available.

3256/-344/20261.name: FUEL OIL HOT
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the fuel oil tempeture becomes excessive. Could be caused by an engine overheat or the FUEL/OIL heat exchanger not working properly. Or both

3256/-344/20261.name: INLET ICING
3256/-344/20261.data: The inlet is icing

3256/-344/20261.name: OVERHEAT
3256/-344/20261.data: When any overheat condition exists. Systems include: engine compartment, enviromental control system/air conditioning components, avionics bays/components and other monitored equipment.

3256/-344/20261.name: EEC
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the Electronic Engine Control (EEC) is not operating in the normal mode. This system includes fuel flow and engine scheduling. This light can come on when the EEC is no longer controlling the engine in primary mode. Also caused by EEC failure, loss of normal EEC control, and sensor or input failure affecting EEC operation

3256/-344/20261.name: BUC
3256/-344/20261.data: Means the engine has switched to backup control mode. Caused by EEC failure, or loss of normal electronic engine control.

3256/-344/20261.name: AVIONICS FAULT
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the avionics system detects a malfunction in one of the aircrafts avionics subsystems. The specifc fault will be displayed in the PFLD.

3256/-344/20261.name: EQUIP HOT
3256/-344/20261.data: When excessive tempeture is detected in the avionics equipment cooling system. During ground ops, this is normally seen when electrical power is applied without an AC cart attached. During flight this is a sign that the equipment AC system is not working properly. Potentially showing a fault in the heat exchange.

3256/-344/20261.name: RADAR ALT
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the radar altimeter system detects a malfunction, fails or provides invalid altitude data. The radar altimeter measures the aircrafts height above the terrain directly below the aircraft.

3256/-344/20261.name: IFF
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the IFF interrogator/transponder equipment fails, the IFF system detects internal fault, or loss of proper IFF operation (cannot transmit or respond to interrogations)

3256/-344/20261.name: NUCLEAR
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when consent circuitry required for nucealr weapons release fails, a malfunction in the nuclear weapons control or monitoring equipment, or if the aircraft cannot properly communicate with or control the nuclear weapon interface.

3256/-344/20261.name: SEAT NOT ARMED
3256/-344/20261.data: When the seat is not armed.

3256/-344/20261.name: NWS FAIL
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates if the NWS system itself fails, loss of hydraulic pressure to steering system, or if the control circuitry or components that command NWS fail

3256/-344/20261.name: ANTI SKID
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the anti skid system fails, wheel speed sensor fails or provides invalid data, or if the system cannot properly control brake pressure modulation. This alerts the pilot that the wheels make lock or drift during braking.

3256/-344/20261.name: HOOK
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the arresting hook is not locked or is extended. Could illuminate if there is an issue with the button or circuitry related to the button.

3256/-344/20261.name: OXY LOW
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when the LOX supply is nearly depleted (less than ~0.5 liters)

3256/-344/20261.name: CABIN PRESS
3256/-344/20261.data: Illuminates when there is a loss of cockpit pressure and the enviromental control system cannot maintain cabin pressure. The light also turns on if the cabin pressure regulator fails or if the air conditioning/pressurization system fails preventing correct cockpit pressure.

3287/-309/20053.data: Tells the indicator what to show

3287/-309/20053.name: Fuel Quantity Selector
3287/-309/20053.data:
6 position selector switch 
 TEST - AL/FR point to 2000 pounds (±100), totalizer to 6,000 (±100) pounds, and both fuel low caution lights illuminate. 
 NORM - AL indicates sum of aft reservoir and A-1 fuselage tank. FR indicates sum of forward reservoir, F-1 (bladder), and F-2 fuselage tanks. 
 RSVR - AL indicates aft reservoir. FR indicates forward reservoir 
 INT WING - AL indicates left internal wing tank. FR indicates right internal wing tank. 
 EXT WING - AL indicates left external wing tank. FR indicates right external wing tank. 
 EXT CTR - AL drops to zero. FR indicates external centerline tank.

3287/-309/20053.name: EXT FUEL TRANS
3287/-309/20053.data:
NORM - Centerline tank transfers first then external wing 
 WING FIRST - External wing tanks transfer first then external centerline tank.

3431/-167/20139.data: The right MFD is programmable screen

3431/-167/20139.name: FCR
3431/-167/20139.data: Fire Control Radar. Air to air radar display

3431/-167/20139.name: HSD
3431/-167/20139.data: Horizontal Situation Display. Map like display that shows navigation, datalink, and threats

3431/-167/20139.name: SMS
3431/-167/20139.data: Stores Management System. Weapons selection and configuration

3431/-167/20139.name: HARM
3431/-167/20139.data: High Speed Anit-radiation Missile. When using AGM-88

fuel.data:
s//THEORY OF OPERATION//s 

u//Engine Feeding//u 
The engine is fed by the main fuel line located in the right strake. The fuel is fed from the aft and forward reservoirs by 3 boost pumps into the Fuel Flow Proportioner (FFP) to decide which fuel tank system to feed from to balance the aircraft. From the FFP it goes into the Fuel/Oil heat exchanger which cools hydraulic oil, main gen oil, and ADG oil and heats up fuel. After the fuel passes through the heat exchanger, it goes to the main fuel shutoff valve (controlled manually by a switch in the quick access panel or by the FUEL MASTER switch in the cockpit. See cockpit panel chart), then to a fuel flow transmitter (for FUEL FLOW indicator), then to the engine fuel system.


 u//Transfer//u 
 There are two fuel systems, the forward right and the aft left. The forward right system includes: 
 - F-1 
 - F-2 
 - Forward Reservoir 
 - Right Internal Wing 
 - Right External wing 

 The aft left system includes: 
 - A-1 
 - Aft Reservoir 
 - Left Internal Wing 
 - Left External Wing 


During engine operation, the forward system feeds in this order: 

Right external wing -> right internal wing -> F-2 -> FWD reservoir
F-1 -> FWD reservoir 

The centerline feeds into the refuel line, filling up any internal tank that isn't full (basically acting as a portable ground refueler).

The aft system feeds in this order: 

Left external wing -> left internal wing -> A-1 -> Aft reservoir 

For both external to internal wing transfers, there are transfer shutoff valves used for both refuel and engine operation. The centerline does not have one (its gravity filled so it uses back pressure). The wing internal tanks have a fuel pressure driven transfer pump that feed into the corresponding fuselage tank previously laid out. The F-1 fuel tank has an electrical transfer pump that feeds to the FWD reservoir (pump light #1 in 3308). The F-2 tank uses tank pressure to feed to FWD reservoir. The A-1 has an electrical transfer pump that feeds the aft reservoir (pump light #5 in 3308). The reservoirs have 3 electrical boost pumps that feed the FFP (#2 boost pump on the aft, #3 and #4 on the forward) 


u//Pressurization//u 
The entire fuel system is pressurized on warm air from the Environmental Control System (ECS) or from the ground cooling receptacle. The direct source of the air pressure can be found in ECS system page. 

The air comes in from the ECS through a solenoid valve (connects to the halon reservoir in case of fire), then into two solenoid valves that control pressure. There are also two vent & pressure valves (one for internal tanks, one for external) and a remote sensing pressure relief valve. The warm air goes from the ECS system to the wing internal tanks and all external tanks. As fuel gets used, it gets distributed throughout the system.


u//Indication//u

Each fuel tank has a float switch that shows how much is in each tank. Information about the needle positions and indication logic can be found in cockpit page on the FUEL QUANTITY MANAGEMENT panel.

fuel.name: FFP
fuel.data:
The Fuel Flow Proportioner splits fuel between the aft left and the forward right system. It is driven by two constant displacement pumps powered by A system hydro to maintain the center of gravity. Two check valves are in both main lines in the FFP to prevent cross feeding. It is "tuned" so it takes equal amounts from each system.

There is also a bypass in with two check valves in case the FFP fails to ensure the engine still gets fed. There is a pressure switch that shows if its working and is transmitted to the bottom right light in door 3308. In rare occasions during launch, that light can flicker. Tell the pilot to run up the engine to ensure the pressure switch is not bad.

fuel.name: Pumps
fuel.data:
The 6 green lights in door 3308 are for boost pumps, transfer pumps, and the FFP.
 - Light 1: Transfer pump from the F-1 to the forward reservoir
 - Light 2: Boost pump from the aft reservoir to the FFP
 - Light 3-4: Boost pump from the forward reservoir to the FFP
 - Light 5: Transfer pump from the A-1 to the aft reservoir
 - Light 6: FFP pressure switch

There are also two more fuel pressure driven transfer pumps on both the internal wing tanks (pump 6 on the right wing and 7 on the right wing).

A small amount of fuel is sent to the DEC (GE-100/GE-129) or the DEEC (PW-220/PW-229) for cooling.

fuel.name: Halon
fuel.data:
Halon is meant in case of fire in the fuel system. It is controlled by TANK INERTING switch on the fuel panel in the cockpit. 

When the TANK INERTING switch is set to TANK INERTING, it opens two solenoid valves. One right on the halon reservoir, and one right after the halon/air mixing valve. After the first solenoid valve, it goes to the halon/air mixing valve, then gets split to go to the left wing and to the second solenoid valve. After the second solenoid valve, it goes to the fuel tanks. It never goes into the forward or aft reservoir.

fuel.name: Engine Feed
fuel.data:
The engine fuel coming from the main fuel line, uses the engine driven fuel pump (on the engine driven gearbox), to push fuel into the injectors.

The after-burner fuel pump is driven by engine bleed air. It does not run unless the engine is in after burner

hyd.data:
s//THEORY OF OPERATION//s

u//A System//u

The A system controls all the main functions of the hydraulic system. It controls:
 - Flight Controls
 - FFP
 - LEFs
 - Speed Brakes

The hydraulic fluid starts in the reservoir on the right side. From there, the fluid goes through the engine driven hydraulic pump and the EPU hydraulic pump. After that, it goes through the pressure filter, then distributed to the components through a main pressure line. On the filter manifold there is a pressure switch (for the HYD/OIL PRESS light on the right eyebrow in the cockpit) and a pressure transmitter (for the pressure indicator in the cockpit and in the hydraulic system quick access panel). Connected to that main pressure line is the flight control accumulator. After the main pressure line, the fluid goes to the dump and relief valve, then back to the reservoir

The main hydraulic pressure line is always circulating fluid, regardless of what hydraulic components are being operated. The component and its system decided what to do with that circulating fluid.

The fluid returning from the components goes into the main return hydraulic line. The main return line has two ends, one connecting to the dump and relief valve, and one going to the return filter. On the filter is a bypass valve in case the filter is clogged. That bypass line goes directly to the EPU hydraulic pump and engine driven hydraulic pump. After the return pump, the fluid goes to the Fuel/Oil heat exchanger. There is also a thermal bypass before the fuel/oil heat exchanger that will open if the hydraulic fluid is too cold. From the fuel/oil heat exchanger, the fluid goes back to the reservoir.

The A system powers all the main components for flight because, in case both hydraulic systems fail, the EPU hydraulic pump can power the required components for 10-15 minutes so the pilot can find a place to land.


u//B System//u

The B system works exactly the same as the A system, just with more components and a bigger reservoir. It powers:
 - Flight Controls
 - Landing Gear
 - Brakes
 - JFS 
 - LEFs
 - AR Door
 - Gun
 - Nose Wheel Steering

The B system is primarily on the left side, except when distributing power to components.


u//EPU//u

In case BOTH hydraulic pumps fail, the EPU hydraulic pump will take over. The EPU powers the A system hydraulics, which is why the A system only powers components needed for flight. If the A system pump fails, it still has B system. If B system fails, A system takes over, hopefully not in a dogfight or the pilot is hosed. If both fail (or drop below 1000 psi), then the EPU automatically turns on. It can also be manually activated.

hyd.name: Brake/JFS
hyd.data:
The brake/JFS system is powered by the B system. It has its own dedicated filter in the right wheel well. This filter has no bypass. 


u//JFS//u

The JFS system has two modes (START 1 and START 2). START 1 uses one JFS/Brake accumulator, START 2 uses both JFS/Brake accumulators. The JFS has a rotary actuator that uses the accumulator to start the JFS. When this happens, fuel is injected into the JFS and is ignited. When the JFS reaches a desired RPM, the pilot will set the throttle to Idle. When that happens, the clutch that connects the JFS to the ADG will close and transmit power through the ADG, through the PTO shaft, through the engine driven gearbox, and then starts to rotate the engine. Fuel is then injected and ignited, starting the engine.


u//Brake/Anti-skid//u

When the brakes in the cockpit are used, a signal is sent to the brake control/anti-skid assembly. That controls the brake shutoff valves, parking brake valve, metering valves and reads wheel speed transducers. The fluid starts from the B system and is split in two for each brake line, the JFS hand pump, and to the JFS. Each brake line goes through the JFS/Brake accumulators, then to two shutoff valves. Which shutoff valve used depends on which channel the pilot has set it to. From the shutoff valve, it goes through the metering valve (which decides how much pressure to give the brakes from the amount of pressure the pilot has on the pedals), then through a shuttle valve, then to the brake actuators.

The parking brake, set by the PARKING BRAKE switch being set to parking brake, actuates the park valve based on the conditions that the WOW switches are engaged, and the throttle is at or near idle. The pressure is fed into the parking brake valve, to the shuttle valve and prebrake restrictor valve (uses LG UP pressure as a backup to WOW switches), then to the brake line shuttle valves.

The anti-skid system reads the wheel speed transducers to decide if the one or both the wheels have locked. Then it relieves pressure to the brakes, allowing them to spin.

hyd.name: Filters
hyd.data:
u//Pressure//u

The pressure filter is at the start of the system, directly from the pump. It is the furthest outboard filter in both wheel wells. This is the only filter, that if the delta P is popped during launch and is unable to be reset, requires a shutdown and the filter needs to be replaced. 


u//Return//u

The return filter is for the fluid returning from components, right before it goes into the Fuel/Oil heat exchanger. It is located in between the pressure filter and the case drain filter. If the delta P pops during launch and is unable to be reset, the jet can fly but the filter must be replaced/inspected after the flight.


u//Case Drain//u

The case drain filter is for the hydraulic fluid that is inside the hydraulic pump (meant for cooling and lubrication). It is located on the inboard side of the wheel well and is smaller in diameter than the pressure and return filter. If this pops during launch and is unable to be reset, then the jet can fly and the filter must be replaced/inspected after flight. 


u//JFS/Brake//u

The JFS/Brake filter is for the return fluid for both JFS and brake system. It is located on the inboard wall in the left wheel well. The delta P is on top. If this pops during launch and cannot be reset, replace/inspection after flight.

env.data:
s//THEORY OF OPERATION//s

In the environmental system, there are three types of air: cold, warm, and hot. The following is the use cases for all types of air.


u//Hot Air//u

Hot air comes from the high compression section of the engine. Public sources say this air can be up to 1,000 degrees F. The hot air gets turned into warm air via a heat exchanger in the ram air inlet. Hot air is only used to get turned into warm air and as a way to speed up the process of warming the warm air on startup. The hot air goes through a modulating valve that is connected to a warm air tube, and that is controlled by a temp/pressure switch.


u//Warm Air//u

Warn air is sourced from engine bleed air (or hot air) and is cooled via the regenerative heat exchanger (regen). This air is used for fuel tank pressure and, on Pratt and Whitney jets (block 42, 52, and 72), for the engine augmenter air pressure.

After warm air comes out of the heat exchanger (turning hot air to warm air), it split into two paths. One goes to air conditioning system; one goes into the Turbine Compressor. After the turbine compressor, it goes to another heat exchanger that turns it into cold air. 


u//Cold Air//u

Cold air is sourced from the ram air intakes on the top if the engine inlet. After that it goes through another heat exchanger, then to the turbine compressor (there is a warm air path that is connected right after the turbine regulated by a modulating valve and that valve is controlled by a temp/pressure sensor right after water separator), then to water separator. The water from the water separator is what is used in the heat exchanger just mentioned. After that the air gets split into two paths. One goes to the avionics equipment; one goes to the air conditioning system.

env.name: Cockpit Air Conditioning
env.data:
The air conditioning system air comes from right after the water separator. Which is split into the cockpit air conditioning and the equipment cooling system. The cockpit air conditioning line gets heat from a warm air line, controlled by a modulating valve. Another modulating valve controls that main air conditioning line/cabin pressure. 

From there it gets split into four paths for four vents in the cockpit. Two in the front and two in the back.

env.name: Avionic Equipment Cooling
env.data: The avionics equipment cooling comes from a combination of ram air and cold air. The ram air is controlled by a shutoff valve, then gets connected to the cold air line coming from the water separator. In there as well, is the ground cooling receptacle. After all those lines combine, it goes into a modulating valve, then a temp/pressure sensor that is used for the EPUIP HOT light on the fault panel in the cockpit. The final step is to go through a shutoff valve and into the equipment bay.

env.name: Anti-G Suit/Canopy seal
env.data: The Anti-G suit and canopy seal air power comes from the line right after the heat exchanger that uses water from the water separator. Before the turbine compressor.

ele.data:
u//Main Generator//u

The main generator is powered by the ADG through the CSD. The CSD maintains a consistent speed to ensure the generator outputs a consistent power.

When the main generator starts providing power, it goes through two main power contactors which provides power to its AC buses. If they are closed, it lets power from the main gen to flow to the AC buses, if they are open, it uses external power or moves to the standby generator.

On one main power contactor, the AC power moves to the nonessential AC bus #2 (right strake AC power panel) and the overcurrent sensing contactors then to the nacelle nonessential AC power bus (right nacelle equipment bay AC/DC power panel). Then after that it goes into a contactor that is only opened if the standby generator takes over. After that it goes to the essential AC bus, which gives power to the emergency AC bus #2 through another contactor that only opens if the EPU generator takes over. 

Now it moves out of the right strake AC power panel and to an AC to DC converter, which powers the emergency DC power bus #2. The emergency DC bus #2 goes to the ESS DC bus, both the battery busses (1 and 2), and to the converter/regulator (which powers the flight control computer C/D).

On the other main power contactor, the power goes straight to the overcurrent sensing contactors. After power passes through that it goes to nonessential AC bus #1 (forward AC power panel). That moves through a contactor that only opens when the standby takes over, and through another contactor for the EPU generator. 

Then it moves out of the forward AC power panel, through an AC to DC converter, then to emergency DC bus #1. That gives power to the convert/regulator for the FLCC (A/B) and moves to both battery buses. It also moves to a contactor that is only on when the EPU generator is on or standby generator is on (except during ground tests). Through that contactor it goes to a nonessential DC bus that powers nacelle nonessential DC bus #1 and #2. 


u//Standby Generator//u

The standby generator splits to the ESS AC bus and the emergency AC bus #1. It also goes to the two converter/regulators for the FLCC.


u//EPU Generator//u

The EPU generator flows through the contractors going to emergency AC bus #1 and #2. It is controlled by the EPU controller. From the EPU generator, the power goes to an AC-to-DC converter, then to the FLCC (A/B/C/D).
